title: The Resilience Fund is self-insurance Sky controls outright rather than coverage purchased from an insurer
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1 defines the Resilience Fund as "a self-insurance instrument fully controlled by Sky Governance, which will cover legal defense expenses in case of legal or regulatory action against Sky or active participants in the Sky Ecosystem," and designates it "the primary source for direct legal defense funding."

Choosing self-insurance over a purchased policy follows from the risk being close to uninsurable in the conventional market: pseudonymous contributors, a novel regulatory surface, and no legal entity to name as the insured. A.2.9.1.1 keeps the door open — legal defense resources "can include both Sky Governance-controlled assets and external third-party resources" over time — so the fund is a first layer, not a permanent substitute for cover.

The cost of self-insurance is that the risk stays on Sky's balance sheet with no transfer of tail risk. A.2.9.1.1.1.1.1 caps exposure at 5,000,000 USDS per year "with the full amount available at the start of each calendar year," which bounds the loss but also means a single large multi-year action could exhaust a year's capacity and leave later claimants unfunded.

Control also cuts both ways. "Fully controlled by Sky Governance" means no insurer can deny a claim on technical grounds — and equally that no external party is obliged to pay one.
